author: jracer15
body:
I have this friend I know IRL and whenever we try playing on different servers.  The other say I suggested playing on Avicus but he said something that struck my attention.  He said that the server isn't very inviting to new players.  He elaborated that when he was on the server he was treated differently that say some Avicus vets.  I told him that's natural but explained that even on other servers where there are vets it never seems to have cliques that don't invite others to play.  He had a hard time explaining, but he finds that if he was to be in an argument with a well-known person and him and a mod was to figure out the story, they would listen to the well knowns instead.

How do you feel about this?  Do you find Avicus to be a welcoming place?  Do you think we can work on ways to be a more approachable server?

replies.author: Silentdawnslight
replies.body:
Honestly, something as simple as a book with a brief overview of the game in your inventory during spectator mode (+between matches) or elsewhere within the game's own server would be more effective in my opinion. Something they could easily refer to without having to go back to the main hub and everything. And it would be separate for each gamemode.

If you do have something in the hub, I would suggest keeping it separate for the different gamemodes as having it all together can be more confusing for the player. Though I imagine most players would have an easier time understanding when the game is in front of them.

Just keeping it short and simple, let them discover the details on their own, because that's part of the fun!

replies.author: SnowSX3
replies.body:
Avicus is very cliquey at times.

There're a ton of groups of people. It doesn't help in regards to opening up to newer players.

Lets take the Resistance for example.
The Resistance was a small group of people who wanted to change the staff team for the better. I respect their morals but the way they went about achieving their goals was all wrong. Instead of working with the staff team to help improve it, they isolated themselves from the staff and tried to inflict change from over the fence.

It didn't work. Why?
Because they Practiced division instead of practicing unity.

If they had just brought their ideas and criticisms to the staff team directly then they would have achieved some of the change that they wanted.
Instead they just created a divide that ended up hurting themselves, the staff team and the community.
It just didn't work.
 
This example can be used in this new player introduction scenario. 
We have so many small groups of people it could be hard for newer players to fit in at times.

Not saying this is the case for everyone, it's just something I've noticed over the months while using an example that people are familiar with.
